title: Comprehensive cover
summary: Our highest level of motor cover, protecting your own car as well as other people's property.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Accidental damage, fire, theft and malicious damage to your vehicle, plus your liability to third parties under the Road Traffic Act.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Wear and tear, mechanical breakdown, unlicensed drivers and any loss caused by driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

sections.label: Costs and excess
sections.body: You pay the compulsory and any voluntary excess on each claim; the premium depends on your rating factors at quote or renewal.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Report the incident through My Insura or our motor claims line; we appoint an approved repairer and agree the repair estimate.

title: Third party, fire and theft
summary: A middle level of cover that insures damage you cause to others plus loss of your car through fire or theft.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Liability for injury and damage to others, and loss of or damage to your car caused by fire, theft or attempted theft.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Accidental damage to your own car where you are at fault, and damage from vandalism that is not linked to an attempted theft.

sections.label: Costs and excess
sections.body: Premiums are usually lower than comprehensive; excesses apply to fire and theft claims and are shown on your policy schedule.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Report theft to the police first and give us the crime reference number before we can open a theft claim.

title: Third party only
summary: The minimum cover required by law, protecting you against claims from other people but not paying for your own car.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Your legal liability for injury to other people and damage to their vehicles or property, up to the limits in your policy.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Any loss of or damage to your own vehicle, including theft, fire and damage you cause yourself.

sections.label: Costs and excess
sections.body: The lowest-priced level of cover, though some drivers find comprehensive is similar in price after rating factors are applied.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Tell us promptly about any incident involving another party and do not admit liability or agree a settlement without us.

title: Excesses explained
summary: The compulsory and voluntary excess are the amounts you pay towards a claim before we pay the rest.

sections.label: What is an excess
sections.body: The amount you contribute to a claim; it is made up of a compulsory excess set by us and any voluntary excess you choose.

sections.label: Choosing a voluntary excess
sections.body: A higher voluntary excess usually lowers your premium but means paying more if you claim, so pick an amount you could afford.

sections.label: Young and inexperienced driver excess
sections.body: An additional compulsory excess may apply where the driver is under 25 or has held a licence for less than a year.

sections.label: When the excess is not charged
sections.body: Windscreen repair, and claims where we recover all our costs from the at-fault party, may carry no excess in the end.

title: Breakdown cover
summary: An optional add-on that sends a patrol or recovery vehicle if your car breaks down or will not start.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Roadside repair, recovery to a local garage or home and onward travel, depending on the level of breakdown cover chosen.

sections.label: Levels of breakdown cover
sections.body: Roadside only, national recovery and national recovery with at-home start are offered; each adds distance and call-out benefits.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Repairs after the roadside visit, parts, fuel, and breakdowns within the first 24 hours of the policy starting.

sections.label: How to use your cover
sections.body: Call the breakdown line on your card with your policy number and exact location; keep the vehicle somewhere safe while you wait.

title: Courtesy car
summary: An optional add-on providing a small replacement vehicle while your car is being repaired after a claim.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: A small hatchback for as long as an approved repairer has your car after a valid claim, subject to availability.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Cars lent while a claim is investigated, after theft where the vehicle is a total loss, or for non-approved repairers.

sections.label: Conditions of use
sections.body: The courtesy car driver must be named, hold a full licence and meet the hire company's age and deposit requirements.

sections.label: Adding or removing the courtesy car
sections.body: Change this cover at any time through My Insura; the premium adjusts from the date of the change.

title: Motor legal expenses
summary: An optional add-on helping with legal costs to pursue uninsured losses after an accident that was not your fault.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Legal costs of pursuing claims for uninsured losses and personal injury, and defence of certain motoring prosecutions, up to the policy limit.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Disputes with us, claims you cause, and cases our panel solicitors assess as having less than a reasonable chance of success.

sections.label: The legal helpline
sections.body: A 24-hour helpline offers initial advice on motor-related legal problems; it gives general information rather than representing you.

sections.label: How to make a legal expenses claim
sections.body: Contact us before instructing a solicitor so that our panel can accept the case and agree costs in advance.

title: Windscreen cover
summary: Cover for repair or replacement of damaged windscreens and windows, which usually carries a reduced excess.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Repair or replacement of the windscreen, side and rear windows, including fitting and the cost of replacement seals.

sections.label: Repair or replace
sections.body: Chips smaller than a two-pence coin outside the driver's line of sight are normally repaired rather than replaced.

sections.label: Excess and no-claims discount
sections.body: A glass claim carries a lower excess and, with comprehensive cover, does not usually affect your no-claims discount.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Book through our glass partner using My Insura or the claims line; repair can often happen at home or work.

title: Named drivers
summary: Adding other people to your policy so they can drive your car with your insurance in place.

sections.label: Who can be named
sections.body: Any licensed driver aged 17 or over, though their age, history and claims record can change your premium.

sections.label: Adding or removing a named driver
sections.body: Use My Insura to add or remove a driver; changes take effect on the date you choose and may adjust your price.

sections.label: Driving other cars
sections.body: Some policies include limited third-party cover for named drivers in cars they do not own; check your policy wording.

sections.label: Named driver and no-claims discount
sections.body: A named driver does not earn their own no-claims discount unless the policyholder is the main driver, and they should not be misrepresented as the main driver.

title: Young and newly qualified drivers
summary: How cover works for drivers under 25 or who passed their test in the last two years.

sections.label: Why young drivers pay more
sections.body: Insurers rate drivers under 25 and those new to driving as higher risk, which increases premiums and excesses.

sections.label: Learner driver cover
sections.body: Short-term cover lets a learner practise in a family car for days or weeks without affecting the main policyholder's no-claims discount.

sections.label: Pass Plus and driver training
sections.body: Completing an approved course such as Pass Plus may qualify for a discount on some policies.

sections.label: Ways to reduce the cost
sections.body: Choosing a smaller engine, a higher voluntary excess, a telematics policy or being named on a parent's policy can help.

title: Business use and commuting
summary: What counts as social, commuting or business use of your car and how this affects cover and price.

sections.label: Social, domestic and pleasure
sections.body: Covers everyday personal use but not travel to a regular place of work or any use connected with a business.

sections.label: Commuting
sections.body: Add commuting if you drive to a fixed workplace; it is a higher class of use, so you will need to tell us.

sections.label: Business use
sections.body: Use for visits to clients or carrying tools is business use; carrying goods or passengers for hire needs specialist cover.

sections.label: Telling us about a change
sections.body: Tell us as soon as your use changes; failing to do so could lead to a claim being reduced or declined.

title: Driving abroad
summary: Cover for taking your car to other countries, including green card requirements and breakdown abroad.

sections.label: Minimum cover abroad
sections.body: Most policies give at least the legal minimum cover in other countries for up to 90 days a year, though not full comprehensive cover.

sections.label: Extending to comprehensive abroad
sections.body: Ask us to extend to full cover for a trip; this may be free or charged, depending on destination and length.

sections.label: Documents to carry
sections.body: Take your driving licence, vehicle registration document and a green card or insurance certificate where one is requested.

sections.label: If you break down or crash abroad
sections.body: Contact us and any breakdown provider quickly; keep receipts and police reports to support your claim.

title: How your no-claims discount works
summary: The discount you earn for each claim-free year, and what happens to it if you make a claim.

sections.label: Earning your discount
sections.body: You earn one year for each full year you hold a policy without a claim where we pay out and cannot recover our costs.

sections.label: What happens when you claim
sections.body: A claim you are at fault for normally reduces your discount by two years, or sets it back to a lower step.

sections.label: Using a company car or other vehicle
sections.body: Time driving another car as a named driver or on a company vehicle may sometimes count, if you hold written proof.

sections.label: Discount if you stop driving
sections.body: Your discount is usually valid for two years after a policy ends, so you can restart cover without losing it.

title: Proof of your no-claims discount
summary: How to get a letter or document showing how many years of claim-free driving you have earned.

sections.label: Where to find your proof
sections.body: Download your current proof from the Documents area of My Insura at any time during the policy.

sections.label: Proof after you cancel
sections.body: When a policy ends we issue a final proof showing the years earned, normally within five working days.

sections.label: Information on the letter
sections.body: It shows the policyholder, the number of years, the dates of cover and whether the discount is protected.

sections.label: If your proof is lost or wrong
sections.body: Ask us for a replacement through secure messages; we will reissue the document at no charge.

title: Protected no-claims discount
summary: An add-on that lets you make a limited number of claims without losing your discount.

sections.label: What protection does
sections.body: You can make up to two at-fault claims in three years without your discount step falling, though your premium may still rise.

sections.label: Cost of protection
sections.body: Pricing depends on how many years of discount you hold; it is shown separately at quote and renewal.

sections.label: When it does not apply
sections.body: Protection may not apply to a claim after a conviction for a serious driving offence or a lapse in cover.

sections.label: Adding or removing protection
sections.body: Change this on My Insura; you will be asked to confirm that you have no claims you have not told us about.

title: Black box and app-based insurance
summary: Insurance where a device or smartphone app measures how you drive and rewards safer habits with a lower price.

sections.label: How telematics works
sections.body: A small device or our app records speed, braking, cornering, time of day and mileage, and scores each journey.

sections.label: Your driving score
sections.body: Scores are reviewed monthly; a consistently good score earns a premium reduction at renewal.

sections.label: Mileage and night driving
sections.body: Policies set a mileage limit, and regular driving between midnight and 5am may reduce your score.

sections.label: Fitting, returning and privacy
sections.body: A fitter installs the box free; return it within 30 days if you cancel; data is kept as described in our privacy notice.

title: Buildings insurance
summary: Cover for the structure of your home: walls, roof, floors, fixed fittings and outbuildings.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Damage to walls, roof, floors, windows, fixed baths and kitchens, plus garages and fences, from insured causes such as fire and storm.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Wear and tear, gradual deterioration, faulty workmanship and damage you cause by neglecting maintenance.

sections.label: Rebuild cost and sum insured
sections.body: Your sum insured should equal the cost of rebuilding the property, not its market value.

sections.label: Mortgage lender requirements
sections.body: Most lenders require buildings cover from completion; send them your schedule from My Insura.

title: Contents insurance
summary: Cover for belongings inside your home such as furniture, electronics, clothes and carpets.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Furniture, appliances, clothing, jewellery up to single-item limits, and items stored in a locked garage or shed.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Money above the cash limit, items left unattended in gardens, and loss without evidence of ownership.

sections.label: Calculating your sum insured
sections.body: Add up replacement-as-new values room by room; underinsuring may reduce any claim payment.

sections.label: Home contents away from home
sections.body: Items taken outside the home have limited cover unless you add personal possessions cover.

title: Buildings and contents together
summary: A single policy covering both the building and what is inside it, often at a lower combined price.

sections.label: Benefits of combining
sections.body: One renewal date, one excess to pay in many cases, and a combined discount compared with buying separately.

sections.label: When to choose separate policies
sections.body: Tenants only need contents; owners with a leasehold flat may find the freeholder already insures the structure.

sections.label: Excess on a combined claim
sections.body: A single claim affecting both building and contents normally carries only one excess.

sections.label: Switching to combined cover
sections.body: Add buildings or contents through My Insura; your new schedule shows the combined sums insured.

title: Escape of water
summary: Cover for damage from water that escapes from pipes, tanks or appliances.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Sudden damage from escaping water from plumbing, heating systems, washing machines and dishwashers, including drying-out costs.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: The cost of repairing the burst pipe itself, gradual leaks, and flooding from rivers or the sea.

sections.label: What to do straight away
sections.body: Turn off the water at the stopcock, switch off electricity if safe, photograph damage and call us.

sections.label: Trace and access
sections.body: We pay reasonable costs to find the leak and make good the walls or floors opened up.

title: Accidental damage
summary: Optional protection for sudden, unexpected damage to your home or belongings that is not covered elsewhere.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Sudden physical damage to buildings or contents caused by an accident, such as breaking a window or damaging a television.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Damage by pets, wear and tear, cosmetic scratches, and breakage while an item is being repaired or cleaned.

sections.label: Buildings and contents versions
sections.body: Accidental damage can be added to buildings, contents or both, with separate excesses.

sections.label: Claiming
sections.body: Describe how the damage happened; we may ask for photos and a repair quote.

title: Theft and burglary
summary: Cover for items stolen from your home and damage caused by thieves breaking in.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Stolen contents and damage to doors, windows and locks caused by forced entry or an attempt to break in.

sections.label: Security conditions
sections.body: Approved locks on external doors and windows may be a condition; check your schedule for the requirements.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Theft by someone you let in, or where no evidence of forced entry exists and your policy requires it.

sections.label: What to do after a break-in
sections.body: Report to the police, get a crime reference number and ring our claims line promptly.

title: Storm, flood and weather
summary: Cover for damage to your home from storms, flooding, snow and heavy rainfall.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Damage caused by storm winds, rising water from rivers or rainfall, and the weight of snow, including fences and gates in some cases.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Damage to gates, hedges and fences from storms unless your cover specifically includes them; gradual seepage.

sections.label: Flood-risk areas
sections.body: We may apply a higher excess or exclusions in high-risk areas; Flood Re can help with cover for homes built before 2009.

sections.label: Alternative accommodation
sections.body: If you cannot live at home after an insured loss, we pay reasonable rent and living costs.

title: Subsidence, heave and landslip
summary: Cover for movement of the ground beneath your home that damages the building.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Damage to the building caused by the ground sinking, rising or sliding, usually under buildings insurance.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Damage from poor construction, settling of new buildings and damage to boundary walls unless the main property is damaged.

sections.label: Higher excess
sections.body: A subsidence excess usually applies, commonly £1,000, in addition to the standard compulsory excess.

sections.label: Reporting cracks
sections.body: Tell us as soon as you see cracks; we may arrange monitoring and a structural survey.

title: Frozen pipes and heating
summary: Cover for damage caused when pipes freeze and burst, and conditions about keeping your home heated.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Damage from frozen pipes or tanks bursting, subject to the conditions around heating while the property is unoccupied.

sections.label: Unoccupancy conditions
sections.body: If the home is empty for more than 30 days, cover for frozen pipes and some other perils may be restricted.

sections.label: Preventing freezing
sections.body: Keep the heating on low, drain down the system if leaving for a long time and know where the stopcock is.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Contact us as soon as it is safe, with photographs and a plumber's report if available.

title: Alternative accommodation
summary: Help with living costs if you cannot stay in your home after an insured incident.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Reasonable rent, hotel costs and extra living expenses while your home is uninhabitable after an insured event.

sections.label: Limits and time
sections.body: Cover is usually capped at a percentage of the buildings sum insured or a set number of months.

sections.label: Receipts and evidence
sections.body: Keep receipts for accommodation and meals; we only pay costs above your normal living expenses.

sections.label: Landlord's rent loss
sections.body: Landlord policies can pay lost rent while the property is being repaired, if rental income cover is included.

title: Personal possessions outside the home
summary: Optional cover for valuables such as phones, cameras and bikes when you take them out.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Named items you carry away from home, such as mobile phones, cameras, laptops and cycles, for loss, theft or damage.

sections.label: Items over the single-item limit
sections.body: Valuables above the limit must be listed individually with a description and value.

sections.label: Cycling cover
sections.body: Cycles are covered when locked to an immovable object with an approved lock, or when kept indoors.

sections.label: Making a claim
sections.body: Report theft to the police, give the serial number or IMEI and provide proof of purchase.

title: Home emergency and legal cover
summary: Optional add-ons for emergency call-outs such as boiler failure and for legal disputes about your home.

sections.label: Home emergency cover
sections.body: Pays for emergency callouts for problems like no heating in winter, a blocked drain or a broken external door.

sections.label: Legal expenses cover
sections.body: Helps pay legal costs for disputes with contractors, neighbours or tenants, subject to prospects of success.

sections.label: What is not covered
sections.body: Planned maintenance, routine servicing, and pre-existing faults known before the cover started.

sections.label: Using the helplines
sections.body: Call the 24-hour numbers on your policy documents with your policy number ready.

title: Landlord insurance
summary: Cover for owners who let property, including buildings, contents and loss of rent.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Buildings, landlord's contents, public liability and optional loss of rent or alternative accommodation for tenants.

sections.label: Tenants and unoccupied periods
sections.body: Cover is tailored to the type of tenant, and extended empty periods between lets may need to be declared.

sections.label: Malicious damage by tenants
sections.body: Optional cover pays for damage caused deliberately by tenants, subject to conditions and evidence.

sections.label: Telling us about changes
sections.body: Tell us if you change tenants, let to students or sublet, as this may affect cover.

title: Renters' contents insurance
summary: Cover for tenants for their own belongings and for accidental damage to a landlord's fixtures.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Your own belongings, and optionally accidental damage to the landlord's fixtures and fittings.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: The building itself, which the landlord must insure, and loss of items in shared areas.

sections.label: Deciding how much cover
sections.body: Count the replacement value of everything you own that you would not want to lose.

sections.label: Moving out
sections.body: Cancel or transfer the policy when you leave; tell us your new address in advance.

title: Single trip cover
summary: Cover for one holiday or journey, from the day you book until you return.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Emergency medical costs, cancellation and curtailment, delayed baggage and personal liability for the dates of your trip.

sections.label: Start and end dates
sections.body: Cover for cancellation starts when you buy the policy; all other sections start on the trip departure date.

sections.label: Trip length limits
sections.body: Single trip policies cover trips up to 31 days in most cases; longer trips may need extended cover.

sections.label: Buying after you have booked
sections.body: Buy as soon as you book to be covered if you must cancel for an insured reason.

title: Annual multi-trip cover
summary: Cover for all your trips in a year, with a maximum length for each trip.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Every trip you start in the policy year, up to the maximum trip length shown in your schedule, in the countries you selected.

sections.label: Maximum trip length
sections.body: Typically 31 or 45 days per trip; longer trips need an extension or a separate policy.

sections.label: Who is on the policy
sections.body: Individual, couple, family and group policies are available, with all travellers named.

sections.label: Is annual cover worth it
sections.body: It usually pays off from the second trip a year, particularly for European holidays and business trips.

title: Family and group cover
summary: One travel policy for adults and children on the same trip.

sections.label: Who counts as a child
sections.body: Children under 18, or under 23 in full-time education, may be included at no extra cost when travelling with an adult.

sections.label: Group sizes
sections.body: Groups of up to ten adults can be covered together provided everyone travels on the same itinerary.

sections.label: Excess for families
sections.body: One excess applies per person per claim; the schedule shows the amounts for each traveller.

sections.label: Adding a child later
sections.body: Contact us to add a new baby or foster child; there may be no additional premium.

title: Emergency medical cover
summary: Cover for urgent medical treatment, hospital stays and repatriation if you are ill or injured abroad.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Hospital treatment, doctor fees, ambulance, and medical repatriation to the UK, up to the medical limit on your policy.

sections.label: Calling the emergency assistance team
sections.body: Contact our 24-hour team before incurring large costs or agreeing to treatment, so we can arrange payment directly.

sections.label: GHIC and EHIC
sections.body: A UK Global Health Insurance Card gives access to state treatment in the EU but does not cover private care or repatriation.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Treatment that could wait until you return home, and costs of routine or planned procedures.

title: Pre-existing medical conditions
summary: How to declare an existing health condition so that it is covered.

sections.label: What counts as pre-existing
sections.body: Any medical condition you have been diagnosed with, treated for or had symptoms of before the policy starts.

sections.label: How to declare
sections.body: Answer the medical screening questions honestly; you may be offered cover with an extra premium or exclusions.

sections.label: If your health changes
sections.body: Tell us if you receive a new diagnosis or change treatment between buying and travelling.

sections.label: What happens if you do not declare
sections.body: A claim relating to an undeclared condition can be reduced or refused.

title: Cancellation and curtailment
summary: Cover for the cost of a trip you must cancel or cut short for an insured reason.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Unrecoverable travel and accommodation costs if you cannot travel or must return early because of illness, bereavement or jury service.

sections.label: Cancelling for illness
sections.body: A doctor's certificate is needed, and you should cancel the trip as soon as you know you cannot travel.

sections.label: Insured reasons
sections.body: Examples include serious illness or injury, redundancy, and damage to your home that needs you at home.

sections.label: Not covered
sections.body: Changing your mind, financial hardship that is not redundancy, and most airline strikes known before you book.

title: Travel delay and missed departure
summary: Compensation for long delays and for missing a departure because of an unexpected event.

sections.label: Delay payment
sections.body: A fixed sum is payable after the first 12 hours of delay at the departure point, then for each further 12 hours.

sections.label: Missed departure
sections.body: We cover extra travel and accommodation costs if you miss a departure because of a vehicle breakdown or accident.

sections.label: Evidence to keep
sections.body: Get written confirmation of the delay from the airline or carrier and keep all receipts.

sections.label: Airline compensation
sections.body: Claiming from the airline under flight compensation rules is separate; we may ask whether you have done so.

title: Baggage and personal possessions
summary: Cover for lost, stolen or damaged luggage and items such as phones and cameras.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Loss, theft or damage to baggage and personal possessions, with a single-item limit and an overall limit.

sections.label: Delayed baggage
sections.body: Emergency purchases of toiletries and clothes are covered if your bags are delayed for more than 12 hours.

sections.label: Valuables and gadgets
sections.body: Items such as cameras and phones have special limits and must not be left unattended.

sections.label: Reporting loss
sections.body: Tell the police within 24 hours of theft and the airline of loss in writing, and keep reports.

title: Winter sports cover
summary: An add-on for skiing, snowboarding and other snow sports, including piste closure and equipment.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Medical treatment for winter sports injuries, mountain rescue, lost ski pass and hired equipment.

sections.label: Piste closure
sections.body: A fixed daily amount is payable if lack of snow closes the piste for more than 24 hours.

sections.label: Off-piste skiing
sections.body: Off-piste is covered only when accompanied by a qualified guide and within the marked boundaries.

sections.label: Adding winter sports
sections.body: Choose the add-on at quote, or add it later through My Insura before departure.

title: Adventure activities and hazardous sports
summary: Cover for activities such as scuba diving, trekking and bungee jumping that standard travel policies exclude.

sections.label: Included activities
sections.body: Cover includes low-risk activities like snorkelling, easy hiking and cycling on road without competition.

sections.label: Activities needing an add-on
sections.body: Diving to 30 metres, trekking above 3,000 metres and white-water rafting need the activities add-on.

sections.label: Not covered
sections.body: Professional or competitive sport, and any activity where you did not follow safety instructions.

sections.label: Declaring an activity
sections.body: Tell us before you travel; an unexpected extra premium is better than a declined claim.

title: Cruise and long-stay cover
summary: Cover tailored to cruise holidays, missed ports and trips longer than 31 days.

sections.label: Cruise cover
sections.body: Includes cabin confinement, missed port and itinerary change, and emergency medical evacuation from the ship.

sections.label: Long-stay cover
sections.body: Single-trip policies for up to 12 months with set limits for baggage and cancellation.

sections.label: Medical for older travellers
sections.body: Cover is available for travellers over 80 subject to screening and a higher medical premium.

sections.label: Making a claim at sea
sections.body: Obtain a written report from the ship's medical centre before disembarking.

title: Level and decreasing term life cover
summary: Cover that pays a lump sum if you die within a set term, either level or reducing over time.

sections.label: Level term cover
sections.body: The amount paid on death stays the same for the whole term and suits protecting a family's living costs.

sections.label: Decreasing term cover
sections.body: The payout reduces over time in line with a repayment mortgage and is usually cheaper than level cover.

sections.label: Choosing a term and amount
sections.body: Match the term to your mortgage or until children are independent, and the amount to debts plus income needs.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Death from suicide in the first year, and claims where health or lifestyle was not disclosed accurately.

title: Whole of life cover
summary: Cover that pays out whenever you die, as long as premiums are paid.

sections.label: How it works
sections.body: Premiums are paid for life or until a set age, and a lump sum is paid out on death with no end date.

sections.label: Guaranteed or reviewable premiums
sections.body: Guaranteed premiums stay fixed; reviewable premiums can change at set review dates.

sections.label: Using whole of life for inheritance tax
sections.body: It can be written in trust to provide money for a possible inheritance tax bill.

sections.label: Over-50s plans
sections.body: Simple plans with no medical questions but often a smaller payout and a qualifying period.

title: Joint and family life cover
summary: One policy covering two people, paying out on the first or second death.

sections.label: First death and second death
sections.body: First death pays when the first person dies and ends; second death pays after both have died.

sections.label: Cost compared with two single policies
sections.body: A joint first-death policy is generally cheaper but pays out only once.

sections.label: Divorce or separation
sections.body: A joint policy cannot always be split; consider two separate single policies if you may separate.

sections.label: Changing from joint to single
sections.body: Ask us whether the policy allows conversion; evidence of good health may be required.

title: Critical illness cover
summary: A lump sum paid if you are diagnosed with a serious illness listed in the policy.

sections.label: Conditions covered
sections.body: Typical illnesses covered include cancer, heart attack and stroke, defined in the policy document.

sections.label: Definitions and severity
sections.body: A diagnosis must meet the policy definition; early-stage conditions may pay a partial claim.

sections.label: Waiting and survival periods
sections.body: A claim is paid only if you survive the survival period, usually 14 or 28 days after diagnosis.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Conditions that existed before the policy started, and illnesses not listed or not meeting the definition.

title: Children's critical illness cover
summary: Built-in cover paying a lump sum if your child is diagnosed with a specified condition.

sections.label: What is included
sections.body: Children from 30 days to 18 years are covered for a set list of conditions, with a reduced lump sum.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Contact us with the medical report from the consultant treating your child.

sections.label: Does it end your policy
sections.body: A children's claim usually does not affect your own cover.

sections.label: Limits
sections.body: Children's cover is typically the lower of 50% of your critical illness amount or £25,000.

title: Income protection insurance
summary: Regular payments if you cannot work because of illness or injury.

sections.label: How a claim is paid
sections.body: A monthly payment of up to 60% of your pre-tax income is made after the deferred period until you return to work.

sections.label: Deferred period
sections.body: Choose how long to wait before payments start, from four weeks to one year, to match employer sick pay.

sections.label: Own occupation and suited occupation
sections.body: Own occupation pays if you cannot do your own job; suited occupation pays only if you cannot do any suitable job.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Redundancy, pre-existing conditions and illness caused by drug abuse.

title: Short-term income cover
summary: Payments for up to one or two years if you cannot work through accident, sickness or unemployment.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Monthly benefits for a maximum of 12 or 24 months for each claim, paid after a short waiting period.

sections.label: Unemployment cover
sections.body: Redundancy is covered only if you have been employed for at least six months and are not facing known redundancy.

sections.label: Self-employed customers
sections.body: You will need to provide accounts or tax returns to support a claim.

sections.label: Policy exclusions
sections.body: Pre-existing conditions, voluntary redundancy and any fixed-term contract ending.

title: Writing your policy in trust
summary: How putting a policy in a trust can help money reach the right people faster and may avoid inheritance tax.

sections.label: What a trust does
sections.body: The proceeds are paid to your trustees rather than into your estate, which may speed up payment.

sections.label: Types of trust
sections.body: A bare trust names fixed beneficiaries; a discretionary trust lets trustees decide who benefits and when.

sections.label: Inheritance tax
sections.body: A policy in trust is usually outside your estate for inheritance tax, but rules vary and you should check with an adviser.

sections.label: Using our trust forms
sections.body: Download the trust forms from My Insura and send the signed originals to us; we cannot give legal advice.

title: Changing or ending a trust
summary: How to change trustees or beneficiaries on a policy already placed in trust.

sections.label: Changing trustees
sections.body: Complete our trustee change form signed by all existing trustees and the new trustee.

sections.label: Changing beneficiaries
sections.body: This depends on the type of trust; a bare trust cannot be changed once beneficiaries are named.

sections.label: Documents we need
sections.body: A certified copy of the trust deed and identification for any new trustees.

sections.label: Legal advice
sections.body: Speak to a solicitor if you are unsure; we are not able to advise on tax or legal consequences.

title: Telling us about a death
summary: What to do and what we need when a policyholder has died.

sections.label: Who can contact us
sections.body: A relative, executor or solicitor can tell us; we will speak to you with sensitivity and take care of everything we can.

sections.label: What we need
sections.body: A copy of the death certificate and, for a life policy, the claim form and policy number if known.

sections.label: What happens to the policy
sections.body: Life cover can pay out; car, home and pet policies may be amended or cancelled and refunds sent to the estate.

sections.label: How long it takes
sections.body: Most claims are paid within ten working days once we have all the documents.

title: Making a life insurance claim
summary: How the person dealing with the estate can claim on a life policy.

sections.label: Who can claim
sections.body: The policy owner's executor, trustees or named beneficiaries under a trust.

sections.label: Documents needed
sections.body: The death certificate, claim form, identification, and the grant of probate where applicable.

sections.label: Payment
sections.body: We pay by bank transfer to the executor or trustees once the claim is accepted.

sections.label: Claim decisions
sections.body: We may ask for medical records to check the information given at application.

title: Lifetime pet cover
summary: Our highest level of cover, renewing every year with a vet fee limit that resets annually.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Vet fees for illness and injury up to the annual limit, with ongoing conditions covered for as long as you renew.

sections.label: Annual limit
sections.body: The vet fee limit resets at each renewal, so a long-term condition can continue to be claimed on.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Routine care such as vaccinations and neutering, and conditions that existed before cover began.

sections.label: Premiums as pets age
sections.body: Premiums normally increase as your pet gets older, and a co-payment may apply from age eight.

title: Time-limited and maximum benefit cover
summary: Lower-cost cover that pays up to a set amount per condition or for a limited period.

sections.label: Time-limited cover
sections.body: Pays vet fees for a condition for up to 12 months from the date treatment starts, after which it is excluded.

sections.label: Maximum benefit cover
sections.body: Pays up to a fixed amount per condition; once the limit is reached, no further claims for that condition.

sections.label: Which suits your pet
sections.body: Younger pets with a short lifespan can suit lower-cost cover; breeds prone to chronic problems may need lifetime.

sections.label: Upgrading
sections.body: You can usually upgrade at renewal, but conditions that began under the old policy may then be excluded.

title: Accident-only cover
summary: The most basic level, covering injuries from accidents but not illness.

sections.label: What's covered
sections.body: Vet fees for accidental injury such as fractures and wounds, up to the annual limit.

sections.label: What's not covered
sections.body: Illness, dental disease, and anything not caused by an accident.

sections.label: Who it suits
sections.body: Owners who want protection from major unexpected costs but accept illness costs themselves.

sections.label: Switching to fuller cover
sections.body: Moving to lifetime or time-limited cover usually means new waiting periods and exclusions for existing conditions.

title: Pre-existing conditions
summary: What counts as a condition your pet already has and how it affects cover.

sections.label: What counts
sections.body: Any illness, injury or symptom your pet has had before the start date, whether or not it was diagnosed.

sections.label: How we decide
sections.body: We review the vet history for the last 24 months to identify existing conditions.

sections.label: Bilateral conditions
sections.body: If one side was affected, the other side is excluded too, for example a cruciate ligament in either knee.

sections.label: Can an exclusion be removed
sections.body: Some conditions can be reviewed after 24 months with no treatment or signs, with a vet's letter.

title: Waiting periods
summary: The time between starting a policy and being able to claim for illness.

sections.label: Illness waiting period
sections.body: You cannot claim for illness in the first 14 days of the policy; accidents are covered from day one.

sections.label: Specific waiting periods
sections.body: A cruciate ligament injury may have a 30-day wait, and behavioural therapy a longer wait.

sections.label: Continuing from another insurer
sections.body: Ask us to accept transfer of your cover with no new waiting periods where eligible.

sections.label: Cooling-off
sections.body: You can cancel within 14 days of receiving your documents for a full refund if no claim has been made.

title: Vet fee limits and excess
summary: The maximum we pay per year or per condition and the excess you share on each claim.

sections.label: Annual or per-condition limit
sections.body: Your schedule shows the maximum payable in a policy year or for each separate condition.

sections.label: Excess
sections.body: A compulsory excess per claim applies; a voluntary excess lowers your premium but increases what you pay.

sections.label: Co-payment for older pets
sections.body: From age eight you pay a percentage, usually 10 to 20%, of each claim in addition to the excess.

sections.label: Paying the vet directly
sections.body: With a direct-payment vet we pay them, leaving you to pay only your share.

title: Claiming for vet fees
summary: How to claim for treatment and what documents are needed.

sections.label: How to claim
sections.body: Fill in the online form in My Insura, attach the itemised invoice, and ask your vet to complete their section.

sections.label: Direct claims
sections.body: Some vets can claim directly on your behalf; check with the practice before treatment.

sections.label: How long it takes
sections.body: Most straightforward claims are paid within five working days of receiving all documents.

sections.label: Claims for ongoing treatment
sections.body: Send a new invoice for each visit; we track the total against your annual limit.

title: Dental, routine care and breed-specific cover
summary: What is and is not included for teeth, vaccination, neutering and breed-related conditions.

sections.label: Dental treatment
sections.body: Dental treatment is covered when it follows an accident or illness; routine scale and polish is not.

sections.label: Routine care
sections.body: Vaccinations, flea and worming treatments, neutering and microchipping are excluded unless a wellness add-on is chosen.

sections.label: Breed-specific conditions
sections.body: Some breeds have restrictions on conditions known to be hereditary; see the policy schedule.

sections.label: Wellness add-on
sections.body: Pays a fixed amount each year towards routine treatments, whether or not your pet is ill.

title: Escape of water claim
summary: How to claim for damage caused by a burst pipe, leaking appliance or overflowing tank.

sections.label: What to do straight away
sections.body: Turn off the water at the stopcock, switch off electricity if safe, move belongings, and take photos before clearing up.

sections.label: Making your claim
sections.body: Start online in My Insura or call our home claims line, with your policy number and a description of the damage.

sections.label: What happens next
sections.body: We may appoint a loss adjuster, arrange a leak detection engineer and agree drying-out and repairs.

sections.label: Evidence we need
sections.body: Photographs, plumber's report and receipts for emergency repairs and any items you want to claim for.

title: Burglary claim
summary: How to report a break-in and claim for stolen or damaged items.

sections.label: What to do first
sections.body: Report the burglary to the police and get a crime reference number; do not clean up until we advise.

sections.label: Making your claim
sections.body: Tell us the crime reference number and list what was stolen with approximate dates and values.

sections.label: Proof of ownership
sections.body: Receipts, photographs, serial numbers and bank statements help us settle your claim quickly.

sections.label: Replacement and cash settlement
sections.body: We usually replace items through our suppliers or pay a cash sum if we cannot replace them.

title: Storm and flood claim
summary: How to claim for damage from storm, flooding or snow.

sections.label: Make the property safe
sections.body: Prevent further damage with temporary repairs, such as tarpaulins, and keep receipts.

sections.label: Making your claim
sections.body: Claim online or by phone as soon as you can; in a widespread event, claims lines may be busy.

sections.label: Flood restoration
sections.body: We arrange drying and cleaning and may pay for alternative accommodation while the property is repaired.

sections.label: Fallen trees and fences
sections.body: A tree falling on a building is covered; a tree that has damaged only a fence or hedge may not be.

title: Accidental damage claim
summary: How to claim for sudden accidental damage to your home or belongings.

sections.label: Check you have the cover
sections.body: Accidental damage is optional; your schedule says whether it applies to buildings, contents or both.

sections.label: Making your claim
sections.body: Describe what happened and when; we may ask for photos and a repair estimate.

sections.label: Repair or replace
sections.body: We choose the most cost-effective option, repairing where possible and replacing where not.

sections.label: Excess
sections.body: The accidental damage excess shown in your policy documents applies to each claim.

title: Accident claim
summary: What to do after a crash, and how to report it and start a motor claim.

sections.label: At the scene
sections.body: Check everyone is safe, call 999 if anyone is injured, exchange details and take photographs; do not admit fault.

sections.label: Reporting to us
sections.body: Report the accident through My Insura or our 24-hour motor line as soon as possible, even if you do not intend to claim.

sections.label: Fault and recovering costs
sections.body: If the other driver is at fault we try to recover our costs and your excess from their insurer.

sections.label: Repairs
sections.body: We recommend an approved repairer who guarantees repairs, or you may choose your own garage with our agreement.

title: Theft of your vehicle claim
summary: What to do if your car has been stolen or broken into.

sections.label: Report to the police
sections.body: Report the theft immediately and get a crime reference number before contacting us.

sections.label: Waiting period
sections.body: We wait up to 28 days for a stolen vehicle to be recovered before treating it as a total loss.

sections.label: Keys and documents
sections.body: We will ask for all sets of keys, the V5C logbook and details of any security devices.

sections.label: If the car is recovered
sections.body: Do not drive it; we will arrange recovery and inspection and, if repairable, a repair.

title: Hit and run or uninsured driver
summary: What to do if someone hits your car and drives away or has no insurance.

sections.label: What to do
sections.body: Report the incident to the police within 24 hours and note the registration if you saw it; take photographs of the damage.

sections.label: Making your claim
sections.body: Call our motor claims line with the police reference; we handle the claim under your own policy.

sections.label: Uninsured Driver Agreement
sections.body: Where the other driver is traced as uninsured, we may recover costs through the Motor Insurers' Bureau.

sections.label: No-claims discount
sections.body: If you are not at fault and we recover costs, your no-claims discount is normally unaffected.

title: Windscreen claim
summary: How to report and book a windscreen repair or replacement.

sections.label: Before you book
sections.body: Check you have glass cover on your schedule; some policies include it automatically with comprehensive cover.

sections.label: Book your repair
sections.body: Call our glass partner or use My Insura; mobile fitters can visit your home or work.

sections.label: Excess to pay
sections.body: Pay the glass excess at the time of repair; repair is usually free of excess if it is a chip repair.

sections.label: Effect on your no-claims discount
sections.body: A glass-only claim should not reduce your no-claims discount under comprehensive cover.

title: Total loss and settlement
summary: How we value your car and pay out if it is beyond economic repair.

sections.label: When a car is a total loss
sections.body: When repair costs would exceed the market value, we declare it a total loss and offer a settlement.

sections.label: How we value your vehicle
sections.body: We use the pre-accident market value from trade guides, taking account of age, mileage and condition.

sections.label: Salvage categories
sections.body: Cat S and Cat N describe repairable vehicles that were written off; you may keep the car if you accept less.

sections.label: If you disagree
sections.body: Send evidence such as adverts for similar cars and ask us to review the valuation.

title: Medical expenses abroad claim
summary: How to claim for treatment or repatriation after illness or injury abroad.

sections.label: Before you incur costs
sections.body: Call the emergency assistance team on your card for any hospital admission or if costs may exceed £500.

sections.label: Documents needed
sections.body: Itemised invoices, receipts, medical reports and your passport or booking confirmation.

sections.label: Settlement
sections.body: We pay you or the hospital directly and deduct any excess shown on your schedule.

sections.label: Claims on return home
sections.body: Complete the online travel claim form within 31 days of your return.

title: Lost, stolen or damaged possessions claim
summary: How to claim for luggage, phones, cameras and cash lost or stolen on a trip.

sections.label: What to do abroad
sections.body: Report theft to local police within 24 hours and loss to the airline or carrier in writing.

sections.label: Proof you need
sections.body: Police report, property irregularity report from the airline, and receipts or proof of ownership.

sections.label: Limits and depreciation
sections.body: We apply the single-item limit and a deduction for age and wear on belongings.

sections.label: Passports and cash
sections.body: Replacement of emergency travel documents and limited cash theft are covered, subject to evidence.

title: Cancellation or curtailment claim
summary: How to claim after you cancel or cut short a trip for an insured reason.

sections.label: Tell your travel providers
sections.body: Contact airlines and hotels straight away to cancel and ask what refunds are available.

sections.label: Documents needed
sections.body: Booking confirmations, receipts, a doctor's letter and proof of unused travel costs.

sections.label: Medical certificates
sections.body: For illness, your doctor must complete the medical certificate in our claim form.

sections.label: Settlement
sections.body: We pay the unrecoverable amount up to the cancellation limit, less the excess.

title: Vet fee claim
summary: How to claim for veterinary treatment for an illness or injury.

sections.label: What you need
sections.body: The completed claim form, itemised vet invoice and clinical history from the vet.

sections.label: Direct payment
sections.body: If your vet takes direct claims, show your policy details when you arrive for treatment.

sections.label: Pre-authorisation for big treatments
sections.body: Ask us for pre-authorisation before treatment that is expected to exceed £1,500.

sections.label: Decline and review
sections.body: If we decline a claim, you can ask for a review with evidence from your vet.

title: Lost, stolen or straying pet
summary: What we cover if your pet goes missing or is stolen, including advertising and reward costs.

sections.label: Advertising and reward
sections.body: We contribute to advertising, a reward for return and kennel costs, up to the limit in your schedule.

sections.label: What to do first
sections.body: Report to the police, local vets, rescue centres and microchip database.

sections.label: If your pet is not found
sections.body: After 60 days, we can pay the purchase price or value of the pet if theft is proven.

sections.label: Evidence we need
sections.body: Microchip registration, photos, and proof of ownership such as receipts or vet records.

title: Track your claim
summary: How to see progress, updates and next steps on a claim you have made.

sections.label: Where to see status
sections.body: Sign in to My Insura and open Open claims to see progress, dates and any documents we need.

sections.label: What the stages mean
sections.body: Registered, under review, assessor booked, repair authorised, settlement agreed and closed.

sections.label: Typical timescales
sections.body: We acknowledge claims within one working day and aim to update you at least every ten working days.

sections.label: Contacting your claims handler
sections.body: Use secure messages in My Insura or the number on your claim reference letter.

title: Assessor visits and approved repairers
summary: How loss adjusters, engineers and repair partners deal with your claim.

sections.label: Assessor visits
sections.body: A loss adjuster or engineer may visit to inspect damage and agree the scope of repairs.

sections.label: Approved repairers
sections.body: Our repair partners guarantee workmanship for 12 months and handle the claim paperwork for you.

sections.label: Choosing your own repairer
sections.body: You can use your own, but we must agree the estimate before work begins.

sections.label: If an appointment is missed
sections.body: Contact us to rearrange; contact details are on the appointment email.

title: Settlement offers and payments
summary: How a claim is valued, offered and paid, including cash settlement and excess.

sections.label: How we value your claim
sections.body: We pay the cost of repair or replacement, minus any excess and an allowance for wear and tear on some items.

sections.label: Cash settlement
sections.body: We may offer cash instead of repair at the cost to us of carrying out the work.

sections.label: When you will be paid
sections.body: Payment is made within five working days of agreeing the settlement and receiving your bank details.

sections.label: Underinsurance
sections.body: If your sum insured is too low, the claim may be reduced in proportion.

title: If you disagree with a claim decision
summary: How to ask for a review or complain if your claim is declined or you are unhappy with an offer.

sections.label: Ask for a review
sections.body: Send us your reasons and any new evidence; a different claims manager will review the decision.

sections.label: Make a complaint
sections.body: You can complain at any time; we will respond within eight weeks.

sections.label: Financial Ombudsman Service
sections.body: If you are still unhappy after our final response, you may take your complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service free of charge.

sections.label: Legal action
sections.body: You also have the right to seek legal advice; time limits apply.

title: Your renewal quote
summary: What your renewal invitation shows and how to check, compare and accept it.

sections.label: What the invitation shows
sections.body: Your new premium, last year's premium, the cover and excess, and the date the new term starts.

sections.label: Checking your details
sections.body: Make sure your address, mileage, drivers and cover levels are still correct; errors can invalidate a claim.

sections.label: Auto-renewal
sections.body: Policies renew automatically on the stored payment method unless you tell us you do not want to continue.

sections.label: Shopping around
sections.body: You can compare quotes at any time; you do not have to wait for the renewal date.

title: Why your price changed
summary: The factors that make a premium go up or down at renewal.

sections.label: Factors we use
sections.body: Age, address, vehicle or property value, claims history, mileage, occupation and claims costs across the market.

sections.label: Market-wide cost increases
sections.body: Rising repair costs, theft and inflation can raise prices even when your own circumstances are unchanged.

sections.label: Tax and levies
sections.body: Insurance Premium Tax is included in the price shown and rises when the rate changes.

sections.label: Ways to lower your premium
sections.body: Increase your voluntary excess, remove unneeded extras, pay annually and review sums insured.

title: If we do not offer renewal
summary: Why we might decline to renew and what your options are.

sections.label: Reasons for non-renewal
sections.body: Reasons can include claims history, withdrawal of a product or non-payment; we tell you in writing.

sections.label: What to do next
sections.body: Compare other insurers early; you may need to give details of why cover was not renewed.

sections.label: Your records
sections.body: Ask us for a letter showing your no-claims discount, claims history and cover dates.

sections.label: Challenging a decision
sections.body: Contact us if you think the decision is wrong; you can ask for a manager to review.

title: Multi-policy and loyalty discounts
summary: Discounts for holding more than one policy or staying with us.

sections.label: Multi-policy discount
sections.body: Take two or more eligible policies and receive a discount applied to each premium.

sections.label: Loyalty discount
sections.body: Existing customers may receive a small discount when they renew, shown in the renewal quote.

sections.label: Referral rewards
sections.body: Introduce a friend who buys a policy and you may both receive a voucher, subject to terms.

sections.label: Combining renewals
sections.body: Align renewal dates by contacting us; we can help you spread cost.

title: Promotional codes and offers
summary: How to use a discount code and what conditions apply.

sections.label: Applying a code
sections.body: Enter the code at the quote stage; it cannot be added after you have bought the policy.

sections.label: Conditions
sections.body: Codes may apply only to new customers, specific products or purchases made before a closing date.

sections.label: Cashback and vouchers
sections.body: Cashback is paid within 60 days after the cooling-off period has ended.

sections.label: Existing customers
sections.body: Offers for new customers are not available on renewal; ask us whether a loyalty price is available.

title: Pay monthly or yearly
summary: The ways to pay your premium and how monthly instalments are calculated.

sections.label: Paying monthly
sections.body: You pay a deposit and the balance in monthly instalments by Direct Debit; the credit agreement shows the interest charged.

sections.label: Paying annually
sections.body: One payment by card or bank transfer; usually cheaper overall because no interest is charged.

sections.label: APR and the cost of credit
sections.body: Monthly payments are a credit agreement, with an APR shown on your quote and agreement.

sections.label: Changing how you pay
sections.body: Switch between monthly and annual from My Insura at renewal; mid-term changes may attract a fee.

title: Direct Debit and payment dates
summary: How your Direct Debit works and how to change the date or the account.

sections.label: The Direct Debit Guarantee
sections.body: You are protected by the guarantee; we write to you ten days before the first collection.

sections.label: Changing the date
sections.body: Choose a new collection day in My Insura; we may collect two payments in the month of change.

sections.label: Changing the bank account
sections.body: Set up a new Direct Debit instruction in My Insura; it takes five working days to process.

sections.label: Cancelling the Direct Debit
sections.body: Contact us first; cancelling your Direct Debit without telling us could lead to policy cancellation.

title: Missed or failed payments
summary: What happens if a payment fails and how to catch up.

sections.label: What happens next
sections.body: We try to collect the payment again after seven days and send a reminder before taking any action.

sections.label: Cancellation for non-payment
sections.body: If arrears remain after the reminder period we may cancel the policy and tell you the cancellation date.

sections.label: Catching up
sections.body: Pay the arrears online or by phone; cover continues if payment is received before the cancellation date.

sections.label: If you are in financial difficulty
sections.body: Contact us as soon as possible; we can discuss a payment plan and signpost free debt advice.

title: Refunds and credit balances
summary: How we calculate and pay refunds after cancellation or changes.

sections.label: How refunds are calculated
sections.body: Pro rata for the unexpired period, less any admin fee and any claims paid in the policy year.

sections.label: When refunds are paid
sections.body: Within 14 days of cancellation, to the bank account or card used for payment.

sections.label: Credit on your account
sections.body: Overpayments are held as a credit and used against your next instalment, or refunded on request.

sections.label: Refund after a claim
sections.body: If a total loss claim has been paid, no refund of the premium is usually due.

title: Paying safely and card payments
summary: How we protect your payment details and what to do if you spot a payment you do not recognise.

sections.label: How we protect your details
sections.body: Payments use encrypted pages and card details are tokenised, so we never store your full card number.

sections.label: Payment you do not recognise
sections.body: Check your policy list in My Insura; if you still do not recognise it, contact us and your bank.

sections.label: Changing your card
sections.body: Update your card in My Insura under Payment methods before it expires.

sections.label: Scam warnings
sections.body: We never ask for card details by text message or for payment to a new account by email.

title: Fees and charges
summary: A list of administration fees for changes, cancellation and documents.

sections.label: Administration fees
sections.body: An admin fee applies for new policies and mid-term changes; the amount is in your Insurance Product Information Document.

sections.label: Cancellation fee
sections.body: A fee applies if you cancel after the 14-day cooling-off period.

sections.label: Cost of documents
sections.body: Duplicate documents are free from My Insura; postal copies may attract a small charge.

sections.label: Fee transparency
sections.body: All fees are shown before you confirm a change, and in your policy schedule.

title: Insurance Premium Tax and price breakdown
summary: What is included in your premium and how tax is shown.

sections.label: What is Insurance Premium Tax
sections.body: A government tax added to most general insurance premiums; the rate is shown separately on your documents.

sections.label: Not charged on
sections.body: Some life and long-term protection policies are exempt from Insurance Premium Tax.

sections.label: Your price breakdown
sections.body: View net premium, tax and fees on your schedule in My Insura.

sections.label: Questions about tax
sections.body: We cannot give tax advice; speak to HMRC or an adviser.

title: Change your address
summary: How to tell us you have moved and what happens to your cover and price.

sections.label: How to update
sections.body: Use Change my details in My Insura, or call us; policies at the old address may need changing or cancelling.

sections.label: Effect on price
sections.body: Your premium is recalculated for the new area, property or parking arrangements, and may go up or down.

sections.label: Insuring both properties
sections.body: If you own both homes during the move, tell us so that cover can overlap for a short period.

sections.label: Moving abroad
sections.body: Tell us before you leave the UK; most of our policies only cover UK residents.

title: Change personal details
summary: How to update your name, phone number, email, job or marital status.

sections.label: Name and contact details
sections.body: Update through My Insura; changes of name need a marriage certificate or deed poll.

sections.label: Job or occupation
sections.body: A new occupation can affect price; tell us about any change in how you earn your living.

sections.label: Marital status
sections.body: This is rarely used for rating but we need it to be correct.

sections.label: Why accuracy matters
sections.body: Incorrect details can lead to a claim being reduced or declined.

title: Change your car
summary: Replacing, modifying or changing details of the vehicle insured.

sections.label: Replacing your vehicle
sections.body: Tell us the registration and details of the new car; cover for the old one ends on the date of change.

sections.label: Modifications
sections.body: Report any changes that affect value, performance or appearance, such as alloy wheels or engine tuning.

sections.label: Temporary cover for a new car
sections.body: Policies include limited cover for a replacement vehicle for seven days while you update us.

sections.label: Price effect
sections.body: Your premium is adjusted for the new vehicle and any difference in value is calculated pro rata.

title: Selling or transferring your vehicle
summary: What to do with your policy when you sell, scrap or give away your car.

sections.label: Tell us when it is sold
sections.body: Contact us on the day you sell or scrap the car to end or move your cover; do not just stop paying.

sections.label: Transferring cover
sections.body: We can transfer the policy to a replacement vehicle, and your no-claims discount stays with you.

sections.label: Refund
sections.body: A pro rata refund is paid for any unused cover, less admin fee, if there are no claims in the year.

sections.label: Statutory off-road notification
sections.body: If you keep a car off the road, tell the DVLA, and ask us about cover for storage.

title: Cancel your policy
summary: How to cancel any policy, what you will get back and the fees that may apply.

sections.label: How to cancel
sections.body: Cancel in My Insura or by phone; we need the date you want cover to end and a reason.

sections.label: What you will receive
sections.body: A pro rata refund, less any administrative fee and any claim already paid.

sections.label: Cancelling a policy with a loan or finance
sections.body: If a lender has an interest in your policy, they may need to agree; you should tell them first.

sections.label: Cover you need by law
sections.body: A car must be insured or declared off the road, so arrange another policy before ending the last.

title: Cooling-off period
summary: Your right to cancel within 14 days of buying or renewing and get a refund.

sections.label: Your 14 days
sections.body: You have 14 calendar days from the day you receive your documents, or the start date if later, to cancel.

sections.label: Refund during cooling-off
sections.body: A refund of the premium for the unused period, less a charge for any time you were covered.

sections.label: How to cancel
sections.body: Contact us by phone, in My Insura or in writing; keep a note of when you cancelled.

sections.label: Claims in the cooling-off period
sections.body: If you make a claim, you may not get a full refund and the rest of the premium may be due.

title: Add or change cover levels
summary: How to add extras or switch cover level midway through a policy.

sections.label: Adding extras
sections.body: Add breakdown, courtesy car or legal expenses in My Insura; cover starts from the date you choose.

sections.label: Changing cover level
sections.body: Moving from third party to comprehensive may require a new quote and an administration fee.

sections.label: Changing excess
sections.body: A new voluntary excess will change your premium for the rest of the period.

sections.label: Removing cover
sections.body: Remove an extra and receive a pro rata refund, subject to the conditions of the add-on.

title: Change your home
summary: Telling us about renovations, extensions, new occupants or a change in how the property is used.

sections.label: Building work
sections.body: Tell us before you start major works; some policies require notification of extensions or conversions.

sections.label: Lodgers and sub-letting
sections.body: Taking in lodgers or letting through short-term rental platforms needs to be declared.

sections.label: Working from home
sections.body: Using part of the home for business can affect contents cover and liability.

sections.label: Unoccupied property
sections.body: A home left empty for more than 30 days may need to be declared and conditions may apply.

title: Transfer or change ownership
summary: Changing the policyholder after a sale, divorce or inheritance.

sections.label: Changing the policyholder
sections.body: We can transfer a policy to another person with their details and agreement; the new policyholder is rated afresh.

sections.label: Selling a property
sections.body: Cancel buildings and contents on completion; we cannot cover a property you no longer own.

sections.label: Probate and inheritance
sections.body: Cover continues for a limited time after death while an estate is settled; tell us as soon as you can.

sections.label: Documents
sections.body: We may ask for the sale contract, grant of probate or decree absolute.

title: Mid-term adjustments and fees
summary: How we work out the cost or refund when you change your policy part-way through.

sections.label: How adjustments work
sections.body: The premium is recalculated for the remaining period and any additional or returned premium is shown before you confirm.

sections.label: Admin fee
sections.body: A fee applies to each mid-term change, shown in your documents.

sections.label: Confirmation of changes
sections.body: You will receive an updated schedule within 24 hours of the change.

sections.label: Reversing a change
sections.body: Contact us within 14 days if you change your mind, though a fee may apply.

title: Contact us
summary: Phone, secure message and post contact details for each type of policy.

sections.label: Phone numbers
sections.body: Call 01632 960 100 for general enquiries, 01632 960 200 for claims and 01632 960 300 for new business (fictional numbers).

sections.label: Secure messages
sections.body: Sign in to My Insura and use Messages for non-urgent questions; we reply within two working days.

sections.label: Post
sections.body: Write to Insura Customer Services, 12 Harbour Row, Northfield, NF1 2AB (fictional address).

sections.label: Text relay and BSL
sections.body: Use Relay UK on 18001 followed by our number; a BSL video service is available during opening hours.

title: Opening times and emergency lines
summary: When each line is open and the 24-hour emergency numbers.

sections.label: General lines
sections.body: Open Monday to Friday 8am to 6pm, Saturday 9am to 1pm, closed on Sundays and bank holidays.

sections.label: 24-hour claims lines
sections.body: Home emergency, motor accident and travel medical lines are open every day of the year.

sections.label: Busy periods
sections.body: Waiting times are longer on Mondays and after severe weather; secure messages may be quicker.

sections.label: Calls are recorded
sections.body: We record some calls for training, monitoring and to resolve complaints.

title: Make a complaint
summary: How to complain about a policy, claim or service and what happens next.

sections.label: How to complain
sections.body: Tell us by phone, post, secure message or complaint form; give your reference and what went wrong.

sections.label: What we do
sections.body: We acknowledge within three working days and aim to resolve within eight weeks, keeping you updated.

sections.label: Final response
sections.body: When we reach a final response we tell you the outcome and your right to go to the Ombudsman.

sections.label: Compensation
sections.body: Where we have made a mistake we may offer an apology, put things right and pay compensation for distress or costs.

title: Financial Ombudsman Service
summary: Taking a complaint to the independent Ombudsman after our final response.

sections.label: When you can go
sections.body: After our final response, or after eight weeks if we have not given a final response.

sections.label: Time limits
sections.body: Go within six months of our final response; the Ombudsman may take older complaints in some cases.

sections.label: How it works
sections.body: The service is free and independent; it reviews the case and may order us to pay compensation.

sections.label: Contact details
sections.body: Financial Ombudsman Service, fictional contact details are shown on your final response letter.

title: Report suspicious contact
summary: What to do if someone has pretended to be us or you think you have been scammed.

sections.label: Signs of a scam
sections.body: Unexpected calls asking for card details, texts with links to pay, or emails requesting a change of bank account.

sections.label: What to do now
sections.body: Stop contact, call your bank, change passwords and report to Action Fraud; then tell us.

sections.label: Reporting to us
sections.body: Forward suspicious emails to the address on our website and tell us the number or website used.

sections.label: How we will contact you
sections.body: We will never ask you for your full card number, PIN or password.

title: Insurance fraud and false claims
summary: What counts as insurance fraud and what happens when it is found.

sections.label: What is insurance fraud
sections.body: Deliberately giving false information, exaggerating a claim or staging an accident to obtain money.

sections.label: Ghost brokers
sections.body: People who sell fake policies at low prices; check details on the regulator's register before paying.

sections.label: What we do
sections.body: We investigate suspected fraud, may refuse claims, cancel policies and share information with fraud databases.

sections.label: Reporting fraud
sections.body: Tell us in confidence if you suspect someone of fraud; calls are free and anonymous if you wish.

title: Accessibility and alternative formats
summary: Support for customers who need information in other formats or help using our services.

sections.label: Formats available
sections.body: Large print, Braille, audio, easy read and text-relay support for letters and policy documents.

sections.label: Using our website
sections.body: Our website is designed to work with screen readers and keyboard navigation; see the accessibility statement.

sections.label: How to ask
sections.body: Tell us once and we note it on your account for all future correspondence.

sections.label: Reasonable adjustments
sections.body: We can arrange sign language support and a trusted person to speak on your behalf.

title: Extra support for customers in vulnerable circumstances
summary: How we help if illness, bereavement, financial difficulty or other circumstances make dealing with us harder.

sections.label: Who we support
sections.body: Customers affected by bereavement, health conditions, domestic abuse, financial hardship or other life events.

sections.label: Trusted third party
sections.body: Appoint someone to speak for you; we may need your consent or a power of attorney document.

sections.label: A single point of contact
sections.body: We can assign a specialist to your case so you only tell your story once.

sections.label: Your information
sections.body: We record only what you agree to, and it is used to support you.

title: Your data and privacy rights
summary: How to see, correct or delete the personal information we hold.

sections.label: Requesting your data
sections.body: Make a subject access request by secure message or post; we reply within one month.

sections.label: Correcting or deleting
sections.body: Ask us to correct wrong information, or to delete what we no longer need to keep by law.

sections.label: Marketing choices
sections.body: Change your preferences in My Insura or reply STOP to any marketing text.

sections.label: Complaining to the regulator
sections.body: You may complain to the Information Commissioner's Office if you are not happy with how we use data.

title: My policies
summary: The policies you hold with us, their cover, renewal dates and what to do next.

sections.label: Your policies
sections.body: A list of your active car, home, travel, life and pet policies and their renewal dates.

sections.label: Policy summary
sections.body: The cover, excesses and extras on each policy in plain language.

sections.label: Renew, change or cancel
sections.body: Links to change your policy, add extras or ask us to cancel.

sections.label: Sharing access
sections.body: Add a trusted person to view your policies without giving them your password.

title: Documents
summary: Your policy schedules, certificates, no-claims proof and other documents.

sections.label: Certificates and schedules
sections.body: Download your current certificate of motor insurance and schedule for any policy.

sections.label: No-claims discount proof
sections.body: Download proof of no-claims discount for each car policy.

sections.label: Letters and statements
sections.body: Past renewal letters, payment statements and claim correspondence.

sections.label: Paperless preferences
sections.body: Choose to receive documents only in your account and by email.

title: Open claims
summary: All claims you have started and not yet settled, with status and next steps.

sections.label: Claims in progress
sections.body: Each open claim with its reference, status and the date of the last update.

sections.label: Documents to upload
sections.body: Photos, invoices and forms we still need to progress your claim.

sections.label: Messages from your handler
sections.body: Read and reply to your claims handler securely.

sections.label: Start a new claim
sections.body: Choose the policy and type of incident to start a fresh claim.

sections.body: Reference CLM-HM-20261012-0388, home policy, escape of water, reported 12 October 2026.

title: Saved car renewal quote
summary: Your saved car renewal quote, step 3 of 4 (synthetic test state).

sections.label: Quote summary
sections.body: Comprehensive cover for one car, renewal date 3 December 2026.

sections.label: Progress so far

sections.label: Continue where you left off
sections.body: Choose add-ons and move on to review and payment.

sections.label: Quote validity
sections.body: Your price is held for 30 days from the day you saved it.

title: Saved quotes
summary: Quotes you have saved but not bought.

sections.label: Your saved quotes
sections.body: A list of quotes with the policy type, price and date to buy by.

sections.label: Retrieve with a reference
sections.body: Enter your quote reference and date of birth to reopen a quote.

sections.label: Price validity
sections.body: Quotes are held for 30 days, after which prices may change.

sections.label: Delete a quote
sections.body: Remove old quotes to keep your account tidy.

title: Payment methods
summary: The cards and bank accounts used to pay for your policies.

sections.label: Cards on file
sections.body: View, add and remove payment cards, with the last four digits shown.

sections.label: Bank accounts
sections.body: The account used for Direct Debit instructions for monthly payments.

sections.label: Change payment date
sections.body: Pick the day of the month your instalments are taken.

sections.label: Payment history
sections.body: See each payment, the amount and the date it was collected.

title: Messages
summary: Secure messages between you and Insura, including claims updates.

sections.label: Inbox
sections.body: Messages from us about your policies, renewals and claims.

sections.label: Send a message
sections.body: Start a secure message; choose the topic and attach files up to 10MB.

sections.label: Reply times
sections.body: We aim to reply within two working days, and one working day for claims.

sections.label: Notifications
sections.body: Choose email or text alerts when you have a new message.
